tables.name: users
tables.purpose: Stores identity for the signed-in user and future expansion to multiple accounts.

columns.name: id
columns.notes: UUID or string identifier, e.g. user-123

columns.name: username
columns.notes: Login name for the user. Current MVP uses 'user'.

columns.name: password_hash
columns.notes: Reserved for future auth implementation. MVP login remains frontend-only.

tables.name: boards
tables.purpose: Represents the Kanban board for a user. The MVP keeps a single active board per user.

columns.name: user_id
columns.notes: Current MVP has one board tied to one user.

tables.name: board_columns
tables.purpose: Tracks the fixed columns on the Kanban board and their visible order.

columns.name: title
columns.notes: User-editable display name for the column

columns.name: sort_order
columns.notes: Order of columns in the board

tables.name: cards
tables.purpose: Stores the board's cards and their placement within columns.

columns.name: column_id
columns.notes: Current column assignment for the card

columns.name: sort_order
columns.notes: Order of cards within a column

relationships.users_to_boards: One user may have one active board in the MVP, but the schema is ready for multiple boards per user in the future.
relationships.boards_to_columns: Each board can have many columns. The column ordering is represented by sort_order.
relationships.boards_to_cards: Each board can have many cards. Cards belong to a specific column and retain a card order within that column.
relationships.columns_to_cards: Each column can contain many cards, and each card belongs to a single column at a time.

mapping.column.cardIds: cards grouped by column_id and ordered by sort_order
mapping.card.title: cards.title

notes: The MVP keeps the implementation purposefully simple: one user, one board, fake login in the frontend, and no auth table required yet.
The schema still supports future multi-user growth by storing users separately and allowing one-to-many board ownership.
This model is designed to map cleanly to the existing frontend board state without unnecessary complexity.
